What this drawing shows, and what it does not
Power lite is the robot's battery protection and power distribution; it
replaces the rev B power board (#207). It carries the pack connectors, the
BMS and main-switch pads, the fuses, the E-stop relay and the servo
distribution. Nothing is soldered on the General Driver.
The servo rail is fed through K1 and F1 (15 A). The General Driver and the
Pi are fed through F2 (3 A) and stay up through an E-stop. K1's coil is on
only while the E-stop's NC contact (J11) is closed and the ESP32 holds
SERVO_EN high; until then R2 holds Q1 off and the rail stays off.
ESTOP_N reads low while the E-stop is released and high when it is pressed,
the board is unpowered, F2 has blown or the lead is unplugged: every failure
Each of the four servo branches (J4-J7) is a chain of stock 5264 leads.
Every hop fits the stock 150 mm lead except shoulder to elbow on both arms,
which needs about 200 mm (152 mm with the shoulder fold's loop;
The leg IDs are as assembled (docs/servo-map.md 2.1). Neck and arm IDs 13-17
are still a proposal. Which General Driver port each leg was plugged into
was not checked (servo-map.md); the servo data line is one net, from H5
H6 and H5's DC_IN pin are not used by this harness; the harness tables in
pcb/power-board/harness.md list only J8 to H5 for servo data.
Not drawn or not verified: the physical fan-out of J12 to the General
Driver's headers (harness.md lists it for the rev B board; J12's pins 2, 3,
5 and 6 carry the same signals on power lite, but the header families, check
P5, were not verified); the BMS thresholds (to be measured); the relay's
inrush, set by the pack, BMS and wiring, which bring-up step 3 checks; the
bench current figure with a watt meter.
The old harness's INA219 caveat is unchanged: the board's INA219 sees only
the buck's current, none of the servo current.
